title: Division vs Truncation
objective: Demonstrate the differences between float division (/), floor division (//), and truncation toward zero int(a / b) on positive and negative inputs.
description:
Task: In computer arithmetic, dividing integers can produce different outcomes depending on the division model applied:
1. Float Division (`/`): Performs standard floating-point division.
2. Floor Division (`//`): Rounds down to the nearest mathematical integer towards negative infinity (standard Python behavior).
3. Truncation toward Zero (`int(a / b)`): Discards the fractional part, rounding towards zero.

Given two space-separated integers A and B (where B != 0), compute and print the three values in the exact format shown below. Float division must be formatted to exactly 4 decimal places.
input_format: A single line containing two space-separated integers A and B.
output_format:
Three lines:
Line 1: Float: <float_result:.4f>
Line 2: Floor: <floor_result>
Line 3: Trunc: <trunc_result>
hint_1: Standard float division in Python uses the single slash / operator.
hint_2: Floor division in Python (//) rounds down towards negative infinity, so -3.5 becomes -4.
hint_3: To truncate toward zero for negative numbers, cast the float division result to an integer using int().
reference_solution:
a, b = map(int, input().split())
f_div = a / b
fl_div = a // b
tr_div = int(a / b)
print(f"Float: {f_div:.4f}")
print(f"Floor: {fl_div}")
print(f"Trunc: {tr_div}")

title: Type Inspection & Validation
objective: Classify incoming string tokens as INTEGER, FLOAT, or STRING representations without relying on exception handling.
time_complexity: O(N) where N is token length
description:
Task: Write a classifier that inspects a single string token and determines what fundamental numeric or textual type it represents:
- Print "INTEGER" if the token represents a valid integer (optional leading '+' or '-' followed strictly by one or more digits).
- Print "FLOAT" if the token represents a valid float containing exactly one decimal point (with an optional leading sign, and at least one digit in the string).
- Print "STRING" for all other tokens (alphanumeric text, words, symbols, or multiple decimal points).
input_format: A single line containing a single token without surrounding whitespace.
output_format: Print exactly one of: INTEGER, FLOAT, or STRING.
constraints: 1 <= len(token) <= 50; the token contains only printable ASCII characters and no spaces.
hint_1: Check if stripping an optional leading '+' or '-' leaves only digits using .isdigit().
hint_2: If the token contains exactly one '.', split around it; the token is a FLOAT when each side is empty or all digits (after an optional sign on the left), and at least one digit exists overall.
hint_3: If it fits neither numeric definition, classify it as STRING.
reference_solution:
s = input().strip()
sign_len = 1 if s.startswith(('-', '+')) else 0
body = s[sign_len:]
if body and body.isdigit():
    print("INTEGER")
elif '.' in s and len(s.split('.')) == 2:
    parts = s.split('.')
    left, right = parts
    left_valid = (left[1:].isdigit() if left.startswith(('-', '+')) else left.isdigit()) or (left in ('', '-', '+'))
    right_valid = right.isdigit() or right == ''
    total_digits = sum(c.isdigit() for c in s)
    if left_valid and right_valid and total_digits > 0:
        print("FLOAT")
    else:
        print("STRING")
else:
    print("STRING")

title: Systematic SIP Value
objective: Compute future value of recurring monthly SIP investments using annuity compounding formula.
description:
Task: Compute the maturity value of a monthly Systematic Investment Plan (SIP).
Given:
- Monthly investment P (float)
- Expected annual return rate R in percentage (float)
- Investment tenure Y in whole years (integer value, e.g. 5 or 5.0)

Formulas:
- Total months: n = int(Y * 12)
- Monthly periodic rate: i = (R / 100) / 12
- If R == 0: Maturity = P * n
- If R > 0: Maturity = P * [((1 + i)^n - 1) / i] * (1 + i)
- Total Invested = P * n
- Wealth Gained = Maturity - Total Invested

Output all three values formatted to two decimal places.
input_format: A single line containing three space-separated numbers: P R Y.
output_format:
Three lines:
Line 1: Invested: <inv:.2f>
Line 2: Maturity: <mat:.2f>
Line 3: Wealth Gained: <gain:.2f>
hint_1: Total months n = int(Y * 12). Total invested is P * n.
hint_3: Use the annuity-due formula: multiply P * ((1 + i)**n - 1) / i by (1 + i) at the end. If R == 0 there is no growth, so maturity equals total invested.
reference_solution:
p, r, y = map(float, input().split())
n = int(y * 12)
invested = p * n
if r == 0:
    fv = invested
else:
    i = (r / 100.0) / 12.0
    fv = p * (((1.0 + i)**n - 1.0) / i) * (1.0 + i)
gain = fv - invested
print(f"Invested: {invested:.2f}")
print(f"Maturity: {fv:.2f}")
print(f"Wealth Gained: {gain:.2f}")

title: Coordinated Time Offset
objective: Apply modular arithmetic on 24-hour clock time to handle forward and backward minute offsets across midnight boundaries.
description:
Task: Given a 24-hour time in HH:MM format and an integer offset in minutes (which may be positive, negative, or zero), calculate the resulting time.
Rules:
- The clock operates on a 24-hour cycle from 00:00 to 23:59 (1440 minutes per day).
- Forward offsets roll past midnight (e.g., 23:45 + 30 mins -> 00:15).
- Negative offsets roll back into the previous day (e.g., 00:15 - 30 mins -> 23:45).
- Output the resulting time formatted with two-digit zero padding: HH:MM.
input_format: A single line containing HH:MM time and an integer offset (separated by space).
hint_1: Convert the starting time entirely into total minutes from midnight: H * 60 + M.
hint_2: Add the offset minutes and use Python's modulo operator % 1440 to wrap cleanly across midnight (Python handles negative modulo automatically).
hint_3: Divide back by 60 for new hours (// 60) and modulo by 60 for new minutes (% 60). Format with :02d.
reference_solution:
time_str, offset_str = input().split()
h, m = map(int, time_str.split(":"))
offset = int(offset_str)
total_mins = (h * 60 + m + offset) % 1440
new_h = total_mins // 60
new_m = total_mins % 60
print(f"New Time: {new_h:02d}:{new_m:02d}")
